NPLify · P0 Technical Baseline

Deliverable 1 — Entity-Relationship Diagram & Data Model · Draft v5.3

New XP Technologies Limited

9 October 2026 · Confidential · Internal baseline document

Status and conventions

Status: Draft v5.3 (9 October 2026) applies the thirteen fee-practice decisions D20–D32 and the same-currency rule D33, confirmed by NPL on 8–9 October from the fee table, Sud's workbook answers and the Project Context and Payment methods tabs: volume tiers and per-sender splits (D20, D21), the displayed fee (D22), NPL-GR as an own-desk project (D23), invoices paid in parts (D24), a rounding menu (D25), markup shared with a client party and rebates as their own stream (D26, D27), partner rates as quoted (D28), the bank cutoff and rate lock (D29), cash by token with rates per city (D30), wallet screening (D31), single-use accounts and loss events (D32), and same-currency pass-through (D33). Six tables and two views are added; invariant 3 is restated; invariants 20–32 are new. The amendments of 9 October (D27, D29, D30) are recorded in §6. It carries v5.0–v5.2 (D13–D19) unchanged. Supersedes v5.2, v5.1, v5.0 and v4.0 in full. This baseline is an internal New XP document; the client deliverables are derived from it. Dependent documents have not yet been regenerated against this version (see §6).

Convention: all monetary amounts are stored as exact decimals; every table carries created_at / created_by; audit, approvals and locking are modelled once (domain 4) and apply to all master data. Derived figures (client balance, group entitlement, offsets, custody) are views over postings and deals — never stored.

Seven diagrams across four domains, one schema: 60 tables and 6 views. In each diagram, entities defined in another diagram appear with no attributes and name that diagram. Relationship lines run from the referenced row to the row that stores the foreign key; ||--o{ is composition (the parent owns the child), ||..o{ a reference or a polymorphic link resolved by a type column plus an id. Diagram 3a of v5.2 is split into 3a and 3c in v5.3 because the deal leg and its stamps outgrew one page. Section 6 lists what changed since v4.0; Appendix A reconciles the model with the FRS; Appendix B is the data dictionary.

1 · Configuration domain

A Project (= client) owns its configuration. Partners are global counterparties; how a partner is used in this project is the partner configuration block — fees, vehicles, endpoints, registrations and rebate terms hang off it. Counterparty receivers are organised in receiver groups, the unit entitlement is tracked on, and each receiving entity holds one or more accounts with a currency and rail.

Diagram 1a. PARTNER_CONFIG, PARTNER_PAIR, SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION, FEE_STRUCTURE are defined in Diagram 1b.

Diagram 1b. PROJECT, CURRENCY_PAIR, SENDER, RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT, OWN_WALLET are defined in Diagram 1a.

Notes

  • A Project (= client) owns its configuration. Counterparty receivers sit in receiver groups: every project has one default group and every counterparty receiver belongs to exactly one group. Entitlement is tracked per group, so payouts within a group are ordinary settlement and only payouts across groups are offsets; a project with a single group never has an offset.
  • A Receiver has a kind: counterparty for a client receiver; sender_return stands for a sender so refunds use the ordinary payout path and the partner's destination approval; partner_transit stands for a partner's collection endpoint so the hop of a two-leg route is an ordinary payout. sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group (group_id is null). They never appear on forward deals or allow lists — both validate kind = counterparty — and a payout to them is attributed to the group of the leg that pays them, so no entitlement moves between groups on a refund or a hop. Groups exist for entitlement and offset accounting; refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule, not a group (D13).
  • A receiving entity holds one or more accounts, each with a currency and rail (EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA are two accounts). An account is a bank account or a wallet (account_kind): a bank account carries bank_details_ref and a bank rail; a wallet carries network and address explicitly, mirroring the partner-side COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT, so addresses can be checksum-validated, checked against the rail, and found when the same address is registered with two partners. Registrations and payout lines point at the account. No table stores actual bank details: bank_details_ref points at the external store.
  • Fees are per partner × pair (FEE_STRUCTURE under PARTNER_PAIR), so choosing the partner is part of pricing. PARTNER.disclosure_style records whether the partner's markup is visible; partner_markup_pct is known only for market_plus partners.
  • A partner operates through one or more legal vehicles (PARTNER_ENTITY: PT-tour, PT Global Inc); the deal stamps the vehicle at quote so paperwork names the right company. Each vehicle owns the endpoints a sender can pay into (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT): kind = bank with a currency and bank_details_ref, or kind = wallet with network and address. The partner side therefore mirrors the client side — PARTNER_CONFIG → PARTNER_ENTITY → COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT as RECEIVER → RECEIVING_ENTITY → RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (D15). An endpoint also carries a nullable rail: a bank endpoint must have it before it becomes active, and a wallet may leave it null but must match network when it is set (D18); the endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection_method (D19). Cash-in has no endpoint record; the leg carries the city and the collection the token (D30). The collected cash amount is rounded by the pair's cash_rounding option — truncate, nearest or round up — to cash_rounding_unit (100 / 500 / 1,000 by currency), the same menu as payout rounding (D25).
  • Destination approval is per partner: SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION is an account of the project's receiving entity as registered with this partner, carrying the partner's approval status and the payout details the partner holds. Those details follow the account's kind: bank_details_ref for a bank account, network and address for a wallet (D16). SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY is the narrative on an outgoing transfer; SETTLEMENT_RAIL is the bank/EMI that executes it; neither holds money. COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY is provenance only and never a payout destination.
  • OWN_WALLET exists for rerouting and pass-through (AQN-LT-Sub is an own wallet at Aquanow); PARTNER_CONFIG.applicable_for_reroute defines the alternate-partner set. Under an own-desk partner configuration (is_own_desk, the NPL-GR game-reseller project) NPL itself is the converting party: its pairs are priced market plus NPL's markup and its collection endpoints are NPL's own wallets (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT.own_wallet_id); the custody view reports every such balance (D23).
  • Fees in v5.3. A FEE_OVERRIDE may carry its own sender / receiver split instead of inheriting the structure's proportion (D20). FEE_TIER rows under a structure price by the project's calendar-month volume; a leg that takes the month past a threshold is split across two tiers (D21). displayed_fee_basis / displayed_fee_pct on the structure say what the customer's quote prints when it differs from the recorded parts; the printed "source rate" is derived at quote, never typed (D22). CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding is a menu — truncate, nearest or round up, to the unit or to rounding_unit — and a pair may have the same currency on both sides (D25, D33).
  • Who else earns on a deal. INTRODUCER / REFERRAL_RULE record a share NPL pays — or, with basis share_of_net_markup and party_kind client_party, the customer who provides a sub-account and shares NPL's markup (Raeen): the base is the leg's fee parts less its partner cost, rebates excluded, several parties may hold rules with different shares, and settlement_mode party_retains means the party holds the converted money and pays NPL the remainder monthly (D26). PARTNER_REBATE_RULE records the rebate a partner pays NPL, with a basis (percentage of amount or of the partner's fee) and an optional scope by sender or fee structure; the rebate is NPL's alone and is reported as its own stream (D27).
  • Cutoff, screening, single use. PARTNER.bank_cutoff_time (the partner's own clock, beside its rate expiry and holiday calendar) and PARTNER_PAIR.needs_bank_lock drive same-day or next-day conversion (D29). A cash side of a currency pair names its CASH_LOCATION — INR (Cash-Delhi) → USDT and INR (Cash-Mumbai) → USDT are two pairs — so partner pairs, fee structures and rate days are per city by construction; bank and crypto sides carry no location (D30). WALLET_SCREENING records the screening of a sending or receiving wallet address, by Operations, and the endpoint's risk_band says which decisions may land on it (D31). An endpoint or a receiving-entity account may be single_use, reserved for one deal (ad hoc local deposit accounts, D32).

2 · Rates domain

Diagram 2. RATE_SOURCE, CURRENCY_PAIR are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_PAIR in 1b; DEAL in 3a; CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION in 3c.

Notes

  • The rate comparison for the day is created lazily by the first deal that needs it, one per partner × pair × date, and reused by every deal that day. A partner may give a new rate during the day, so one date can hold several versions. Rolling averages are built from confirmed versions only.
  • A version is breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel); quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with a reason, rejects, or asks for a better rate. Versions are never overwritten; every deal leg, conversion and balance conversion references its exact version.
  • Cross-source slippage is a query over MARKET_RATE across sources for the same pair and window.
  • A version stores the rate as the partner quoted it (quoted_rate, quoted_direction); rate is normalised to the pair's direction and derived — 1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ — so Ali's 1.1738 becomes 0.851934 without a hand inversion, and a direction slip is caught by the breach check (D28). A cash city is its own currency pair (CASH_LOCATION), so Delhi and Mumbai have their own rate days and rolling averages (D30).

3c · Conversion, reroute, earnings receivable, balance conversion, entitlement re-attribution

Diagram 3c. PROJECT, RECEIVER_GROUP, OWN_WALLET are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_CONFIG, PARTNER_PAIR in 1b; PARTNER_RATE_VERSION, MARKET_RATE in 2; DEAL in 3a.

Derived views (never stored)

ViewDefinition
CLIENT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency)CLIENT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency) = Σ conversions’ actual_out booked at that partner (deal legs and balance conversions, target side) − Σ balance conversions’ amount_in (source side) + Σ returned amounts − Σ released disbursement totals. Carries rounding dust below one unit. v5.3 (D29): also reports a pending column — the expected_out of legs whose rate is locked with the partner but whose money has not yet been collected or converted; a void removes it. Pending is never a posting.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency)GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency) = Σ client_net of converted legs (forward and return) attributed to the group ± entitlement re-attributions − Σ DISBURSEMENT_LINE.amount on lines whose disbursing deal is attributed to the group + Σ returned amounts on those lines. A payout to a group-less receiver debits the group of the leg that pays it, read from DISBURSEMENT_LINE.deal_id (v5.0 D13; D17 makes the paying leg a stored column). Σ over a project's groups = Σ CLIENT_BALANCE over partners, per currency.
OFFSET(group, currency)OFFSET(group, currency) = GROUP_ENTITLEMENT; positive = owed, negative = holding another group's flow. Arises only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to another group (v5.0); zero by construction in a single-group project. Carries Management approval and tighter aging.
CUSTODY(own_wallet)CUSTODY(own_wallet) = Σ collections into the own wallet under open reroutes + Σ recovered dues resting there + Σ own-desk client balances (v5.3, D23) − Σ forwarded or paid out; each row with deal, reason, age. The standing control on money in NPL’s hands.
INVOICE_BALANCE(invoice)INVOICE_BALANCE(invoice) = INVOICE.amount − Σ DISBURSEMENT_LINE.obligation_discharged over lines with outcome confirmed. The open part of a vendor obligation paid in another currency, in parts (v5.3, D24).
PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME(project, month, currency)PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME(project, month, currency) = Σ DEAL.amount_in over forward legs of the project collected in the calendar month, in the tier’s volume currency. Read at quote to choose the FEE_TIER; stamped on the leg as tier_volume_basis (v5.3, D21).

Notes

  • Every deal belongs to a deal group. DEAL_GROUP is the client-facing instruction: the pair as the sender sees it, the sender rate, fee, reference and entry mode. A plain single-partner deal is a group of one leg; a route that needs two partners (INR → USDT at Ali, USDT → EUR at Jeton) has two forward legs; a rejected payout is unwound with a return leg.
  • Legs. leg_type forward or return; funding_source collection, prior_leg (leg 2 of a route, no collection) or returned_disbursement (a return leg). Priced once and partner fixed at quote hold per leg. Attribution is to the receiver group: set at quote on the first forward leg, inherited by leg n of a route from leg n−1 and by a return leg from its parent leg. The receiver is optional until settlement.
  • Two entry modes as before: collect-first legs are born in state Collected with priced_at = conversion time; quote-first legs carry sent / valid / grace timestamps and a late decision. An estimate-first mode gives an indicative figure and prices at conversion.
  • Conversion has exactly one owner: a deal leg or a BALANCE_CONVERSION. The receiver-side fee is taken at conversion. Amounts are rounded at conversion by the pair's option (D25); a dropped fraction (rounding_residual, signed) stays client money in the balance and pays out when it reaches a unit, an amount added by rounding up is NPL's cost. NPL's margin is captured at conversion and is never again at risk from a return or a forward.
  • Balance conversion is NPL converting a client's held balance (5K SGD → USDT to fund a 15K USDT payout): Finance-initiated, Management-approved, no sender, receiver or collection, same rate machinery, markup by FEE_DECISION. It names the receiver group it serves; ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION moves that group's entitlement to the new currency, and any excess over the group's entitlement is booked as an approved offset.
  • Reroute is the only way partner or partner entity change after quote. Forwarding is forward_full or forward_and_recover_dues: NPL nets what the alternate partner owes it (EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE) against the funds forwarded, within the outstanding receivable, with the partner's agreement recorded. Post-collection outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender.
  • One settlement model: DISBURSEMENT drains one partner's holding into one or many DISBURSEMENT_LINEs, rounded as the pair says. Under disburse_policy to_zero the balance after release is less than one unit; under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project's exposure cap.
  • A line paying a counterparty receiver whose group differs from the paying leg's attributed group is an offset, created by the same action, with Management approval and tighter aging. A line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver is never an offset: those receivers have no group, and the line debits the group of the leg it names in deal_id (D13, D17).
  • Rejected payout. When the receiving or intermediary bank rejects a transfer, DISBURSEMENT_RETURN records the returned amount, bank fee and reason; the line's outcome becomes returned, a reversing ledger transaction puts the money back into the client's balance and the paying leg's group entitlement, and BANK_FEE_EVENT books the bounce fee. The money then stays in balance for later payouts, or funds a return leg — attributed to the same group — that converts back and pays the sender's return receiver.
  • Fee decisions. FEE_DECISION is a one-off, approved decision on a single subject: markup applied or waived on a return leg or balance conversion, a network-fee override on a refund, a bank-fee treatment override on one settlement. Standing rules stay in FEE_STRUCTURE and FEE_OVERRIDE.
  • CONFIRMATION is full or short; a short confirmation opens a SHORTFALL topped up by a later disbursement or an explicit separate payout — cash found short at hand-over included. Rounding differences no longer land here. REFERRAL_ACCRUAL and PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL accrue per deal under their rules; a party_retains referral accrual is a receivable from the party, reconciled monthly like a rebate (D26); rebates are reconciled monthly against the partner's statement, which covers NPLify deals only (D27).
  • Pricing stamps (v5.3). A leg stamps the override and the base tier that priced it; a leg that crosses a tier threshold holds two DEAL_FEE_TIER portions and a blended fee (D20, D21). The deal group stamps the displayed fee and source rate the quote printed (D22). On a pair that needs a bank lock the leg records rate_locked_at and conversion_due_date: locked before the partner's cutoff it converts the same day, otherwise the next business day at that day's version; the sender's figures are write-once, NPL absorbs the difference as a cutoff-timing variance, and a conversion whose next-day rate breaches the margin is deferred with a reason. The client balance view shows the locked leg's converted value as pending from the lock; a void removes it (D29).
  • Invoices. INVOICE is an obligation in its own currency — a vendor's EUR invoice a reseller customer pays in THB or USDT, in parts, over days. A deal group names the invoice it pays (advance, then balance); each payout line records how much of the obligation it discharged and the market snapshot used; INVOICE_BALANCE is the open remainder (D24).
  • Cash and crypto parts. A cash part carries the token (the local-currency bill whose serial identifies the agent), the agent's contact and the partner's count; the city is on the pair, which is why the rate, the fee and the partner pair are already the city's (D30). A crypto part carries the sender's declared address and the screening that admitted it, unless the project skips up-front screening (D31).
  • Loss events. LOSS_EVENT records money lost after it was verified or released — a frozen local account, cash short that cannot be recovered, a wrong-chain transfer — on either side, by any method, for a partial or full amount, with the loss split across sender, NPL, partner and client; Management approves the split, one reversing transaction posts it, and a collection-side event moves the part to reversed (D32).

4 · Ledger & controls domain

Diagram 4. OWN_WALLET, RECEIVER, SENDER, INTRODUCER are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_CONFIG in 1b; COLLECTION in 3a; DISBURSEMENT, DISBURSEMENT_RETURN, CONFIRMATION, BANK_FEE_EVENT, REFERRAL_ACCRUAL, PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL, LOSS_EVENT in 3b; CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION, REROUTE in 3c.

Notes

  • Client due balances are held as one account per project × partner × currency (CL.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.DUE); group entitlement is a view, not an account. holder_type never includes a settlement rail or narrative entity.
  • Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver, and withholding on a reroute is not a separate event because the margin is always captured by whichever partner converts.
  • Recover dues on a reroute posts own-wallet cash against the earnings receivable at the partner: company money on both sides, no income.
  • Transaction sources: Collection, Conversion, BalanceConversion, Disbursement, DisbursementReturn, Confirmation, BankFeeEvent, Reroute, Referral, Rebate, LossEvent, Adjustment. Account purposes include PAYABLE, REFERRAL_PAYABLE, SHARE_RECEIVABLE, REBATE_RECEIVABLE, EARN_GROSS, EARN_REBATE, EXP_ROUNDING and EXP_LOSS; ADVANCE does not exist. Cost components include referral, share, rebate, rounding, fx_timing, cutoff_timing and loss.
  • Three streams NPL never mixes (v5.3). Earnings on deals post to EARN_GROSS at conversion; a partner's rebate posts to EARN_REBATE and is never in the base a client party shares (D26, D27); NPL's remainder from a party that holds the converted funds sits in SHARE_RECEIVABLE until the party pays it. The cost of rounding up is EXP_ROUNDING, NPL's share of a loss event is EXP_LOSS; the client's and sender's shares of a loss reduce the client balance, the partner's share is a receivable from the partner (D25, D32). Own-desk deals use the ordinary partner-coded accounts with the own-desk configuration as holder and EXP_PARTNER zero by construction (D23).
  • APPROVAL, AUDIT_LOG and RECORD_LOCK are modelled once and apply to all master data. Approver ≠ initiator on every approval; Operations never sees derived economics. Approval actions include refund_to_third_party, cross_group_payout, balance_conversion, recover_dues, enable_own_desk, approve_loss_split and override_screening_reject. cross_group_payout never fires on a line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver. Wallet screening itself is an Operations action, not an approval (D31).

5 · Invariants (enforced at write time)

  1. Postings in one transaction sum to zero per currency.
  2. Ledger tables are append-only; corrections are reversing transactions.
  3. No custody in the normal path: CL.OWN.*.HELD may be debited only by a collection on a deal with an approved REROUTE, or on a leg whose PARTNER_CONFIG is an own desk (v5.3, D23 — the NPL-GR game-reseller project); the custody aging view reports both and is the standing control.
  4. Disburse to the residual: under disburse_policy = to_zero a DISBURSEMENT pays the balance rounded by the pair’s option and leaves only the rounding residual (dust stays client money; a round-up is NPL’s cost — D25); under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project’s exposure cap (Q5, Q8).
  5. Priced once, per leg: a leg’s pricing fields are write-once after priced_at; a re-quote is a new leg or a new deal group.
  6. Partner fixed at quote, per leg: partner_pair_id / partner_entity_id change only through an approved REROUTE. A collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity (v5.1, D15). Its kind must match the leg’s collection_method — wallet for crypto, bank for bank, no endpoint for cash (v5.2, D19). A COLLECTION may reference only an active endpoint; a bank endpoint is active only with rail set (D18).
  7. Entitlement conservation: Σ GROUP_ENTITLEMENT over a project’s groups = Σ CLIENT_BALANCE over partners, per currency, including balance-conversion re-attributions. Return and hop legs preserve this because they inherit the parent leg’s group (D13). Since v5.2 every payout line resolves to a group — the paid receiver’s for a counterparty, the paying leg’s via deal_id otherwise — so this is checkable mechanically (D17).
  8. Destination approval precedes collection: a quote-first deal cannot leave Inquiry unless at least one account in the entitled group has an approved SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION with the chosen partner.
  9. Approver ≠ initiator on every APPROVAL; Operations never receives derived-economics fields.
  10. Every balance shown anywhere is a sum over postings or deals.
  11. A collect-first deal requires an existing SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW entry for its sender and group (Q1).
  12. A return leg pays the sender_return RECEIVER linked to the parent leg’s sender, unless a Management-approved exception with a reason names another approved receiver.
  13. The failed forward line is reversed before a return leg opens, so entitlement and balance are correct at the return conversion.
  14. A CONVERSION belongs to exactly one owner: a deal leg or a balance conversion.
  15. A recovery on a reroute cannot exceed the outstanding EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE at that partner; the alternate partner’s expected conversion is computed on the net amount forwarded.
  16. Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver (Q13).
  17. Offsets arise only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to a different group, and carry Management approval and tighter aging. A project with one group never has an offset; within a group nothing is tracked beyond an informational tally (v5.0).
  18. A RECEIVER has a group_id if and only if kind = counterparty. Forward legs and the sender allow list target counterparty groups and receivers only. A return leg inherits receiver_group_id from its parent leg; leg n of a route inherits it from leg n−1 (v5.0, D13).
  19. A DISBURSEMENT_LINE paying a group-less receiver (sender_return, partner_transit) carries deal_id; the paying leg’s group is a stored fact, never inferred (v5.2, D17).
  20. A FEE_OVERRIDE with its own split has both share columns set and they sum to its pct; with neither set the structure’s proportion applies. The leg stamps the override that priced it (v5.3, D20).
  21. The base tier stamped on a leg is the tier with the highest min_monthly_volume not exceeding the project’s calendar-month volume at quote (PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME); a leg that takes the month past a threshold is split into two DEAL_FEE_TIER portions whose amounts sum to amount_in, and its fee parts are the blended sum (v5.3, D21).
  22. Displayed figures are derived, never typed: displayed_source_rate = sender_rate ÷ (1 − displayed_fee_pct), stamped at quote; the true rates and fee parts are stored beside them and Operations sees the displayed pair only (v5.3, D22).
  23. Σ obligation_discharged over an invoice’s confirmed lines never exceeds its amount; a line that names an invoice names a deal_id whose deal group is on that invoice (v5.3, D24).
  24. Rounding is the pair’s configured option — amount_rounding / rounding_unit on payouts, cash_rounding / cash_rounding_unit on the cash amount collected; the residual is signed — a dropped fraction stays client money in the balance, an amount added by rounding up is NPL’s cost posted to EXP_ROUNDING — so every rounding difference has an owner (v5.3, D25).
  25. Σ pct of the share_of_net_markup rules active on one leg ≤ 100 %; the share base is the leg’s fee parts less its partner cost and never includes a partner rebate. A party_retains accrual is a receivable from the party, reconciled monthly (v5.3, D26).
  26. Rebate income posts only to EARN_REBATE, never to EARN_GROSS, and every rebate accrual names the NPLify deal it arises on; the partner statement is reconciled against those deals alone (v5.3, D27).
  27. A partner rate version stores the rate as quoted and its direction; the normalised rate is derived (1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ, at the pair’s precision) and is subject to the breach check like any other, so a direction slip freezes the pair instead of pricing a deal (v5.3, D28).
  28. On a pair that needs a bank lock, a leg’s conversion_due_date is the lock date when rate_locked_at precedes the partner’s cutoff and the next business day otherwise; Converting may not start before it. The sender’s figures are write-once (invariant 5); the difference between the stamped partner rate and the rate actually used posts to VARIANCE with component cutoff_timing — NPL absorbs it (v5.3, D29).
  29. A currency pair’s cash side names its CASH_LOCATION and a leg’s collection_method is cash if and only if its pair’s from side does (a cash payout if and only if the to side does); partner pairs, fee structures and rate versions are therefore per city by construction. A cash part is verified only after the partner’s count (counted_at) (v5.3, D30, amended 9 October).
  30. A crypto collection names its sending address and, unless the project skips up-front screening, the screening that admitted it; a screening decided accept_alternate may land only on an endpoint whose risk_band is elevated, and no collection exists for a decision of reject unless Finance overrides it (v5.3, D31).
  31. A single_use endpoint or account is referenced by at most one collection or payout line, for the deal it was reserved for, and retires when that reference is verified or confirmed. A LOSS_EVENT’s shares sum to its amount, which never exceeds the amount verified or released; a collection-side event moves the part to reversed and the client balance never goes below zero (v5.3, D32).
  32. A pair whose two currencies are the same is converted at rate 1 like any other pair, so the sender and receiver fee parts are captured at conversion and the balance arithmetic is unchanged (v5.3, D33).

6 · What changed from v4.0

Draft v5.3 (9 October 2026) applies the thirteen fee-practice gaps found between NPL's fee table, Sud's workbook answers and the Project Context / Payment methods tabs and ERD v5.2 — written up as proposals A–M in "Model Gaps & Proposals v1.0" and confirmed by NPL on 8–9 October — plus the same-currency rule, as decisions D20–D33. Six tables are added (FEE_TIER, DEAL_FEE_TIER, INVOICE, WALLET_SCREENING, LOSS_EVENT, CASH_LOCATION) and two views (INVOICE_BALANCE, PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME): 60 tables and 6 views. Earlier: v5.0 / v5.1 (7 October) removed the return group (D13), gave accounts explicit wallet fields (D14) and restructured the partner's collection side (D15); v5.2 (8 October 2026) added D16–D19.

v5.3 — the fee-practice decisions (9 October 2026)

D20 (A) — A per-sender override carries its own split

Decision. FEE_OVERRIDE gains sender_share_pct and receiver_share_pct; both blank means the structure's proportion, both set means they sum to pct. DEAL stamps fee_override_id.

Rejected alternative. Keeping the override as a total only, with the structure's proportion.

Why. Evo's selected senders pay 1.0 % while Evo still pays its 0.6 %; a proportional override would charge 1.12 % and 0.48 %. NPL confirmed the receiver part is fixed for every sender.

D21 (B) — Fees by monthly volume

Decision. FEE_TIER under a fee structure (one tier at volume 0); the tier is chosen at quote from the project's calendar-month volume (PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME) and stamped with the volume that justified it. A leg that takes the month past a threshold is split: DEAL_FEE_TIER holds the portion below the threshold at the lower tier and the portion above at the next, and the leg's fee parts are the blended sum.

Rejected alternative. A rolling 30-day window; switching the whole leg to the new tier; switching from the next leg only.

Why. GDC pays 2.5 % below USD 500,000 a month and 2.25 % above, switched by hand today. NPL: calendar month; the crossing transaction itself attributes the part above the threshold to the lower tier.

D22 (C) — What the quote prints

Decision. FEE_STRUCTURE.displayed_fee_basis (actual / sender_share_on_partner_rate / fixed) and displayed_fee_pct; DEAL_GROUP stamps displayed_fee_pct and displayed_source_rate = sender_rate ÷ (1 − displayed fee) so a re-printed quote matches. Displayed figures are derived, never typed; Operations sees the displayed pair, Finance both.

Rejected alternative. Leaving the recomputation of the 'market rate' to Operations by hand.

Why. BF quotes via Ali show 'fee 1 %' while the recorded parts add to 1.4 % (Ali's 1 % inside its rate plus NPL's 0.4 %). NPL: a BF-only rule, to be cleared when the project moves to partner rate plus markup. The Raeen sub-account quote uses the same recomputation.

D23 (D) — NPL-GR as an own-desk project

Decision. PARTNER_CONFIG.is_own_desk; an own wallet is a COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT under it (own_wallet_id); own-desk pairs are priced market plus NPL's markup with generated rate versions; invariant 3 restated: client money may rest in NPL's wallet under an approved reroute or in an own-desk project, and the custody view reports both. Enabling an own desk is a Management-approved configuration change (enable_own_desk).

Rejected alternative. Keeping the no-custody principle intact and running the game-reseller flows outside NPLify.

Why. The reseller products (Bala, Fair, 66 Group, TripleSeven, Alpha Plus, 27 Group via THB cash) collect into NPL's own wallet and pay vendors from it on later days; there is no outside partner for the conversion. NPL's framing: NPL-GR, a business unit of NPL, is the client. Management confirmed running it inside the system.

D24 (E) — Invoices paid in parts

Decision. INVOICE owned by the project, naming the vendor; DEAL_GROUP.invoice_id; DISBURSEMENT_LINE gains invoice_id, obligation_discharged, discharge_rate and the market snapshot used; INVOICE_BALANCE = amount − Σ discharged over confirmed lines. The EUR difference between what was collected and what was discharged posts to variance with component fx_timing.

Rejected alternative. Tracking the obligation in a free-text client reference.

Why. A vendor's EUR invoice is settled in USDT in instalments at different days' rates (EUR/USDT 0.8708 at collection, 0.87527 at the last payment); the open balance changes with every instalment. NPL: wanted; vendors are paid on different days and the forex difference is accepted within the 2 % markup.

D25 (F) — A rounding menu per pair

Decision. CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding grows from one value to truncate_unit / nearest_unit / round_up_unit / nearest_n / round_up_n with rounding_unit; CONVERSION.rounding_residual is signed — a dropped fraction stays client money, an amount added by rounding up is NPL's cost in EXP_ROUNDING. Cash collections use the same menu on the collected amount (cash_rounding with cash_rounding_unit).

Rejected alternative. Truncation only, with the other practices left outside the system.

Why. Live quotes round THB and INR to the nearest 1,000 and round a reseller customer's USDT up. NPL: round up to the nearest 1,000 for Asian currencies, nearest unit for USD, SGD, HKD; round-up on USDT is deliberate.

D26 (G) — Markup shared with a client party

Decision. REFERRAL_RULE basis share_of_net_markup: the base is the leg's fee parts less its partner cost, on amount × market, rebates never included; party_kind introducer / client_party; settlement_mode npl_pays / party_retains; optional scope by fee structure; several rules per project with Σ shares ≤ 100 %. REFERRAL_ACCRUAL gains direction, period and received_amount; a party_retains accrual is a receivable (SHARE_RECEIVABLE) reconciled monthly.

Rejected alternative. A fixed percentage per party, reconfigured when the route changes; NPL always paying the share out.

Why. Raeen's downlines fund sub-accounts at 4 %; whatever is left after the partner's fee is split equally — 1.5 % each via Ali, 1.6 % each via Aquanow — Raeen keeps the converted EUR in its own Aquanow account and pays NPL monthly; direct downlines split 0.2 % 75 / 25. NPL: future deals may have several parties with different shares; the partner's rebate is NPL's alone and not visible to the party.

D27 (H) — Rebates as their own stream

Decision. Rebate income posts to EARN_REBATE, never EARN_GROSS. PARTNER_REBATE_RULE gains basis (pct_of_amount / pct_of_partner_fee) and pct, retires the old pct_of_partner_fee column (amended 9 October), and gains an optional scope by sender or fee structure. PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL keeps deal_id required and gains statement_ref.

Rejected alternative. Accruals without a deal for clients NPL referred but does not service.

Why. NPL: the partner statement that NPLify reconciles covers only deals NPLify handled — customers working with Jeton or Aquanow directly are out of scope. Jeton pays 0.4 % of the amount on a 1 % or 1.25 % fee and 0.3 % on Novi's 0.9 %, so the rebate is not a fixed share of the fee. Management reads earnings and rebates as two numbers.

D28 (I) — Partner rates as quoted

Decision. PARTNER_RATE_VERSION gains quoted_rate and quoted_direction; rate is derived (1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ, at the pair's precision) and goes through the breach check like any rate.

Rejected alternative. A single normalised rate typed by Operations.

Why. Ali sometimes states USDT → EUR as 1.1738 (EUR-per-USDT the other way round); the hand inversion is a 38 % error waiting to happen, and the audit trail should show the number the partner sent.

D29 (J) — Bank cutoff, rate lock, next-day conversion

Decision. PARTNER.bank_cutoff_time / cutoff_timezone (amended 9 October: on PARTNER, not PARTNER_CONFIG — the cutoff is the partner's, whichever project uses it); PARTNER_PAIR.needs_bank_lock; DEAL and BALANCE_CONVERSION carry rate_locked_at and conversion_due_date (the lock date before the cutoff, else the next business day; Converting may not start earlier) and a conversion_deferred_reason. The client balance view shows a locked leg's converted value as pending from the lock; a void removes it. The difference between the stamped partner rate and the one used posts to variance with component cutoff_timing.

Rejected alternative. Treating the cutoff as part of quote validity; re-quoting the sender the next day.

Why. Evo via Ali: the rate is compared in the morning; locked before 14:30 GMT+8 it converts the same day, otherwise the money is collected on the morning's figures and converted the next business day. AK's USD and SGD balances are banking-ready and wait too. NPL: NPL absorbs the difference; if Ali's next-day rate breaches the margin, ask for a better rate or wait a day; today's balances should show the pending converted value.

D30 (K) — Cash by token, rates per city

Decision. CASH_LOCATION (currency, city, country) named by the cash side of a CURRENCY_PAIR — from_cash_location_id / to_cash_location_id — so INR (Cash-Delhi) → USDT and INR (Cash-Mumbai) → USDT are two pairs and partner pairs, fee structures and rate days are per city by construction (amended 9 October; the first draft put the city on the rate version and the deal); COLLECTION gains token_ref, agent_contact_ref and counted_at, with cash states token_issued → handed_over → counted → verified; DISBURSEMENT_LINE.token_ref for cash payouts.

Rejected alternative. Free-text cash instructions on the deal and one rate per currency; a city column on each rate version and deal (the first v5.3 draft).

Why. A cash collection or settlement is arranged by token — a local-currency bill whose serial number identifies the agent — closed by a photo of the token and the partner's count; INR in Delhi and Mumbai, or USD cash in Bangkok and Singapore, are different agents at different rates.

D31 (L) — Wallet screening

Decision. WALLET_SCREENING per address and day for sending and receiving wallets (result, decision, who, when, evidence); COLLECTION gains sending_address, wallet_screening_id and screening_skipped; COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT.risk_band; SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION.wallet_screening_id. A screening decided accept_alternate lands only on an elevated-band endpoint; a reject is overridden only by Finance.

Rejected alternative. A static risk tier on the sender.

Why. NPL screens the sender's declared wallet before giving out the partner's receiving wallet, routes elevated-risk wallets to alternate wallets, verifies the hash on chain, and screens receivers' wallets before settlement. NPL: screening is a transaction-coordination activity, so it is an Operations action and Operations sees the result. Not every Evo sender accepts up-front screening.

D32 (M) — Single-use accounts and loss events

Decision. COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT and RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT gain usage single_use with reserved_for_deal_id (and an expected amount on the endpoint); LOSS_EVENT on either side, by any method, for a partial or full amount, with the loss split across sender, NPL, partner and client (shares sum to the amount, Management approves); one reversing transaction (source LossEvent); EXP_LOSS; COLLECTION.state reversed. Cash found short at hand-over is a short confirmation topped up at the next settlement or by a separate payout, and a loss event only when unrecoverable.

Rejected alternative. A collection-only reversal borne by the sender in full.

Why. Local deposits use accounts the partner lends for one transaction; a frozen account can lose the funds. NPL: the loss can be partial, can be shared between NPL and the partner as well as the sender, can happen on the settlement side and by other methods, and single-use local accounts are used for settlement too.

D33 — Same-currency pass-through stays in scope

Decision. A CURRENCY_PAIR may have the same currency on both sides; the leg converts at rate 1 so the sender and receiver fee parts are captured at conversion like on any pair.

Rejected alternative. Dropping the dormant Evolution bank-transfer products.

Why. NPL: the fee is still applied because the currency is collected and then settled separately.

Amendments of 9 October (same draft)

D27. pct_of_partner_fee is retired; basis + pct carry the rebate rule. D29. The bank cutoff moves to PARTNER: it is the partner's clock, like its rate expiry and holiday calendar, whichever project uses it. D30. The cash city is a side of the currency pair, not a column on each rate version and deal: CASH_LOCATION is named by CURRENCY_PAIR.from_cash_location_id / to_cash_location_id, so INR (Cash-Delhi) → USDT and INR (Cash-Mumbai) → USDT are two pairs and everything that hangs off a pair — partner pairs, fee structures, rate days — is per city by construction; bank and crypto sides carry no location. Stale wording from before D23, D25 and D26 was corrected in the notes, walkthroughs, invariant 4 and the FRS reconciliation.

Earlier revisions — v5.0 to v5.2

D13 — No return group

Decision. sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group. Attribution of a return or hop leg is inherited from its parent leg. Offsets are defined between a leg's attributed group and the group of a counterparty receiver.

Rejected alternative. A dedicated group of kind = return per project holding the sender_return receivers (ERD v4.0 §6; config schema rule "one default and one return group").

Why. Groups exist for entitlement and offset accounting; refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule, not an entitlement rule, and RECEIVER.kind already enforces it. The return group (a) made every project have at least two groups, so the Understanding document's "a project with a single group never has an offset" was false by construction; (b) classified every refund as a cross-group payout under the v4.0 offset definition, triggering Management approval and offset aging; (c) left the return group's entitlement negative after each refund, breaking invariant 7, unless a reattribution path was added. Removing it restores the Understanding document's §3.3 and §6.3 wording without change. The return group entered during the v4.0 write-up; decision D3 of the review record relied on it and is amended there.

Changed tables

TableChange
RECEIVER_GROUP− kind. A group is a group; exactly one is_default per project (D13).
RECEIVERgroup_id required when kind = counterparty, null otherwise. sender_return and partner_transit receivers never appear on forward deals or allow lists (validation on kind) (D13).
DEALreceiver_group_id: set at quote on the first forward leg; a return leg inherits it from its parent leg, leg n of a route from leg n−1 (D13).
DISBURSEMENT_LINEA line paying a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group and is never an offset (D13).
RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT+ account_kind (bank / wallet); details_ref → bank_details_ref (bank accounts only); + network, + address (wallets only). Write-time rule: a bank account has bank_details_ref and a bank rail; a wallet has network and address and a crypto rail matching the network (D14).

D14 — Explicit wallet fields on receiving-entity accounts. Rejected: keeping wallet details inside the opaque details_ref. Why: the collection side already stored network and address explicitly; the payout side did not, so addresses could not be validated, checked against the rail, or queried across partners. Bank details stay external by reference, as before.

D15 — Partner entity and collection endpoint

Decision. FACILITATING_ENTITY is renamed PARTNER_ENTITY: the partner's legal vehicle whose name appears on paperwork, the mirror of RECEIVING_ENTITY on the client side. COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY (bank-in) and WALLET (crypto-in) merge into one COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT table owned by a partner entity, with kind = bank / wallet and the field shape of RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (rail required only on active bank endpoints, see D18). COLLECTION points at one endpoint (collection_receiving_endpoint_id, null for cash) instead of the hand-rolled endpoint_type + endpoint_id pair. The rename is pending NPL confirmation; the FRS term "Facilitating Entity" stays in Appendix A.1.

Rejected alternative. Keeping two endpoint tables, one with a legal owner (wallets under a vehicle) and one without (bank accounts directly under the partner config).

Why. A bank account is always in some legal entity's name, so the v4.0 split left the schema unable to say which vehicle owns a bank-in account, while every wallet knew its owner. One endpoint table under the vehicle fixes the asymmetry, lets the system check that the account a sender paid into belongs to the vehicle stamped on the deal, removes a polymorphic pair from COLLECTION, and makes the partner side read exactly like the client side: config → entity → endpoint.

TableChange
PARTNER_ENTITYrenamed from FACILITATING_ENTITY; − bank_details_ref (moved to its endpoints).
COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINTnew; replaces COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY and WALLET. partner_entity_id, kind (bank / wallet), currency, bank_details_ref (bank), network + address (wallet), status.
COLLECTIONendpoint_type + endpoint_id → collection_receiving_endpoint_id (null for cash).
DEALfacilitating_entity_id → partner_entity_id.
Invariant 6adds: a collection's endpoint must belong to the leg's partner entity.

v5.2 — decisions of the review of the v5.1 draft (8 October 2026)

D16 — Registration payout details follow the account's kind

Decision. SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION gains network and address (nullable). bank_details_ref ("as paid by this partner") is set only when the registered account's account_kind is bank; for a wallet account the registration carries the network and address as the partner registered them, and the bank field stays empty. The registration remains the partner's view of the destination; RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT remains NPL's.

Rejected alternative. Keeping a bank-only field on wallet registrations (the v5.1 shape).

Why. After D14 and D15 every other destination record is kind-aware; a wallet registration had no field that fitted, so an approved wallet destination either carried no details or carried an address in a field named for bank details. Storing the partner's copy also lets the system compare NPL's record with the partner's before paying to a wallet, where a wrong address is unrecoverable.

D17 — DISBURSEMENT_LINE.deal_id

Decision. DISBURSEMENT_LINE gains deal_id, a nullable foreign key to DEAL: required when the paid receiver is group-less (sender_return, partner_transit), optional on counterparty lines. New invariant 19. GROUP_ENTITLEMENT reads the paying leg's group from it.

Rejected alternative. Leaving the rule in prose ("a payout to a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group").

Why. A DISBURSEMENT pools many deals, and neither it nor its lines named one; the D13 rule and the view that depends on it could not be computed from stored columns, and invariant 7 could not be checked mechanically. The same column will carry the per-line discharge facts of the scenario in which a EUR invoice is paid in USDT in parts.

D18 — Nullable rail on COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT

Decision. The endpoint gains rail, nullable. Null means "not yet known", never "does not matter": a bank endpoint cannot become active — and no COLLECTION or payment instruction may reference it — until rail is set; a wallet endpoint may leave rail null (its network already names the road), and when rail is set on a wallet it must match network (mirrors D14).

Rejected alternative. A NOT NULL rail, which forces a guessed value when a partner sends incomplete details; or no rail at all (the v5.1 shape), which made the "same field shape as RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT" claim inexact.

Why. The road matters on the collection side as much as on the payout side: the same EUR account reachable by SEPA or SWIFT needs different instructions and arrives with different fees; local rails carry transaction limits (UPI caps, RTGS minimums); and a wrong rail recorded with confidence causes the failures a blank cannot.

D19 — Endpoint kind must match the leg's collection method

Decision. A write-time rule, added to invariant 6: a collection endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection_method — wallet for crypto-in, bank for bank-in, and cash-in has no endpoint.

Rejected alternative. None; the rule was missing.

Why. After D15 the fact "how does the money arrive" lives in two places — DEAL.collection_method and the endpoint's kind — and nothing stopped them disagreeing silently.

DISBURSEMENT_LINE+ deal_id — nullable FK to DEAL; required when the paid receiver is group-less, optional on counterparty lines (D17).
COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT+ rail — nullable; required before a bank endpoint becomes active; on a wallet, must match network when set (D18).
COLLECTIONNo column change: may reference only an active endpoint whose kind matches the leg's collection_method (D18, D19).

OFFSETEntitlement − paid per group, arising only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to another group.

Carried over from v4.0 unchanged

The 12 new tables, 16 changed tables and 3 removals listed in v4.0 §6 (INTRODUCER, RECEIVER_GROUP, RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT, REFERRAL_RULE, PARTNER_REBATE_RULE, DEAL_GROUP, BALANCE_CONVERSION, ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION, DISBURSEMENT_RETURN, FEE_DECISION, REFERRAL_ACCRUAL, PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL; the removal of RECEIVER_ENTITLEMENT, withhold_earnings and the ADVANCE purpose) all stand. Of the small gaps noted in the engagement record, cash rounding per currency is closed by D25 and the partner's time zone by D29 (cutoff_timezone); EXCEPTION entity, PARTNER_STATEMENT (a header for the monthly rebate statement would sit above PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL.statement_ref), configuration versioning, SENDER_CREDIT.applied_to_deal_id and DEAL_GROUP.estimate_out remain open.

7 · Open questions

1 of the questions carried from the Understanding document remain open; the rest were answered by NPL in the review of the Understanding document or settled in the ERD reviews of 6–9 October 2026 and are reflected in this draft.

Still open

#QuestionBlocksStatus
9FRS figure reconciliation (1,208 vs 1,225; Mode 1 example)Golden casesSud: Needs clarification. To be discussed.

Answered and reflected in v5.3

#QuestionAnswerIn the model
1Collect-first: must SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW pre-exist for attribution; handling of inbound matching no senderSud: Yes, sender-receiver mapping should be done in configuration. When the transaction is created, the sender is picked from a list.v4.0: write-time rule that a collect-first deal needs an existing allow entry; the allow list now targets receiver groups.
2Withholding-eligibility criteria on rerouted dealsReview (7 Oct): NPL’s cut is always captured at conversion, so it is never at risk from a return or a forward. If forwarding happens before conversion, whichever partner converts captures it.v4.0: the eligibility question dissolves. forwarding_policy is forward_full or forward_and_recover_dues; withhold_earnings is removed. Ownership flips at one event only.
3Post-collection reroute (funds stuck at a partner): transfer, offset, or refund-and-requoteSud: The partner can send the funds to NPL (and NPL decides where to send) or the partner can refund the sender.v4.0: REROUTE.outcome via_own_wallet / refund_sender; a refund is a return leg paying the sender_return receiver.
4Receiving-entity constraints (currency, rail) narrowing settlement choiceSud: Receiving entities have specific bank accounts with currency and rail restrictions, for example EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA.v4.0: RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT; registrations and payout lines point at the account.
5Any deliberate partial-disbursement / reserve policySud: Yes, possible. In some projects the client’s funds sit until they are ready to receive them, within an exposure threshold NPL sets by appetite.v4.0: PROJECT.disburse_policy to_zero / hold_allowed with exposure_ceiling as the cap; invariant 4 restated.
6Receiver-side fee timing per projectSud: Receiver-side fee should be applied at the time of conversion, otherwise the balance will be incorrect.v4.0: default at_conversion; CONVERSION.fee_receiver_part; DISBURSEMENT_LINE.receiver_fee_applied becomes exceptional.
7Network-fee policy on refundsSud: Set at project level with per-transaction override (one 100 USD fee was repaid in the next settlement).v4.0: PROJECT.network_fee_policy plus FEE_DECISION for the override.
8Whole-unit conversion rounding ruleReview (7 Oct): fractions are dropped to whole units at conversion, per transaction (30.152 → 30). The dropped fraction stays client money, carried in the balance and paid out when it reaches a whole unit. Cash collections round to the nearest 100 / 500 / 1000 by currency.v4.0: CONVERSION.rounding_residual; CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding and cash_rounding_unit; disburse to less than one unit; SHORTFALL no longer takes rounding. Superseded in v5.3 by D25: a rounding menu per pair, signed residual, EXP_ROUNDING for round-ups.
10AQN-LT-Sub “settled by offset against transactions outside the system”Sud: This is NPL’s wallet (pass-through at collection or on the settlement side). AQN is Aquanow, a crypto exchange; LT Sub is the account name.v4.0: OWN_WALLET.provider and account_label; pass-through is a two-leg route or a reroute via the own wallet.
11Reference workbooks per project archetypeFee Outlines v0.2 (8 October 2026): every line of NPL’s fee table as a fill-in outline with a worked calculation per transaction pattern, answered by Sud with the Project Context and Payment methods tabs.v5.3: decisions D20–D33 were built from it; the workbook is the acceptance reference for the fee engine.
12FRS P1 / P3 vs rerouting and multi-partner use — amend FRS or restrict scopeSud: Check the added explanations (partner types and channels; pass-through and double conversions in §7.1.1). Ask again if still unclear.v4.0: two-leg routes are deal groups with two legs and a partner_transit receiver for the hop; FRS principles generalised, scope kept.
13Advance funding sourceReview (7 Oct): never. NPL does not pay a receiver before the client’s money has arrived.v4.0: LEDGER_ACCOUNT purpose ADVANCE removed; the advance approval and the “advance” ownership-flip event removed.
14Review point: entitlement split on a balance conversionReview (7 Oct): chosen group, not proportional. The conversion is triggered by a specific payout.v4.0: BALANCE_CONVERSION.receiver_group_id; excess over the group’s source-currency entitlement is booked as an approved offset.
15Review point: refunds to a third party at the sender’s requestReview (7 Oct): allowed by exception only. Default is the sender’s own return receiver; any other destination needs Management approval with a reason and a pre-registered approved receiver.v4.0: invariant on return legs; APPROVAL action refund_to_third_party.
16Review point: recover dues on a rerouteReview (7 Oct): yes, NPL nets what a partner owes it against funds about to be forwarded to that partner.v4.0: forwarding_policy forward_and_recover_dues, recovered_amount, partner_agreement_ref; postings own wallet cash ← earnings receivable, no income.
17Review point: legs of a route share one client-facing quoteReview (7 Oct): yes, a deal group. The sender saw one price and one reference; margin across legs is the group quote minus the partner conversions.v4.0: DEAL_GROUP; every deal belongs to a group, a single-partner deal being a group of one leg.
18Review point (v5.0): does a refund need its own receiver group?Review (7 Oct, New XP): No. Refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule; a dedicated return group made every project multi-group (so “a single-group project never has an offset” was false by construction), classified every refund as a cross-group offset needing Management approval, and left its entitlement negative after each refund, breaking invariant 7.v5.0 (D13): sender_return and partner_transit receivers are group-less; return and hop legs inherit the parent leg’s attribution; offsets are defined only against counterparty groups. New invariant 18.
19Review point (v5.1): restructure the partner collection side — rename FACILITATING_ENTITY, merge the endpoints?Review (8 Oct, New XP): yes. A bank account is always in some legal entity’s name, so the v4.0 split could not say which vehicle owned a bank-in account while every wallet knew its owner. The rename to PARTNER_ENTITY is pending NPL confirmation; the FRS keeps “Facilitating Entity”.D15: FACILITATING_ENTITY → PARTNER_ENTITY (bank_details_ref moved to its endpoints); COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY and WALLET merge into COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT (kind bank / wallet, same shape as RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT); COLLECTION points at one endpoint (null for cash); invariant 6 adds that a collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity.
20Review point (v5.3): can the model express NPL’s fee practice as described in the fee table, Sud’s workbook answers and the Project Context / Payment methods tabs (gaps A–M)?NPL (8–9 Oct): all thirteen confirmed with parameters — receiver part fixed (A); calendar-month tiers, a crossing deal split across tiers (B); displayed 1 % is a BF-only rule (C); run NPL-GR inside NPLify as an own desk (D); invoice tracking wanted (E); rounding menu, round up to 1,000 for Asian currencies (F); markup shared = fee − partner fee, several parties, party holds the funds, rebate NPL’s alone (G); rebates reported apart, statement covers NPLify deals only (H); Ali quotes inverted (I); NPL absorbs the next-day rate difference, pending converted value shown from the lock (J); cash by token, rates by city (K); screening is an Operations action (L); losses partial and shared, both sides, any method (M); same-currency pass-through stays in scope.v5.3, D20–D33: FEE_TIER, DEAL_FEE_TIER, INVOICE, WALLET_SCREENING, LOSS_EVENT; views INVOICE_BALANCE, PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME; invariants 20–32 and invariant 3 restated; purposes EARN_REBATE, SHARE_RECEIVABLE, EXP_ROUNDING, EXP_LOSS.

Partner fixed at quoteSame, except under REROUTEConsistent
